title: MiniMax H3 Open-Source 100-Day Report Card: One Model Spawns 1,472 Models, Downloads Surpass 148 Million

content_html:
After 100 days of open source, MiniMax's H3 has delivered an ecosystem report card: developers have turned one H3 into 1,472 derivative models, corresponding to 1,472 specific needs and use cases, with total downloads exceeding 148 million—more than 17 downloads every second on average, and new derivative models are still emerging in an endless stream. MiniMax summarized this journey as H3Family in a long article and announced that it will continue to open-source and build on the representative community for multimodal creation in the AI era.

H3 has become a starting point connecting enthusiasts, developers, and commercial companies. Global leading tech companies such as NVIDIA, Tencent, and Alibaba; leading AI application platforms such as fal, Suno, HeyGen, Pika, and Creatify; and university teams including MIT, the National University of Singapore, and Hong Kong Polytechnic University have all retrained H3 derivative models in their own directions. More than ten leading companies worldwide have entered into licensing partnerships with MiniMax, laying this foundation into fields such as e-commerce, gaming, film and television, animation, short dramas, and industrial design.

The five “official flagships” in the family each hold their own tier. H3 prioritizes image quality, outputs up to 2K, starts at RMB 0.5 per second, and focuses on “wish-based creation”—it can understand vague inspirations such as the “minimalist fashion” of an ad or the “suspenseful destiny” of a film, and can also make precise continuous adjustments, keeping the image while changing only a person, a piece of clothing, or a patch of lighting. H3-Highspeed takes a balanced route, starting at RMB 0.26 per second; it takes about 11 seconds on average to generate a 5-second video, and videos up to 15 seconds go from prompt to completion in at most 1 minute, with support for up to 30 seconds. H3-Lite focuses on extreme cost-effectiveness, starting at RMB 0.16 per second; on specific hardware, it generates a 5-second 768P video in about 8 seconds for about RMB 1.3, making it suitable for low-cost trial and error in the early stages of creation. On the image side, H3-Image sells itself on the strongest instruction-following ability among open-source models, supports up to 16 reference images, runs at 150%-200% the speed of mainstream models, and costs only 50%-70% as much; H3-Image Highspeed compresses 4K image generation to under 10 seconds, 3-4 times the speed of mainstream models in the same tier.
